hint.SWISS: The scenario is set automatically when the round is generated. Every pairing method avoids rematches and gives a BYE at most once; ELO modes use the global ranking. The BYE takes no table. Tables by standings: the pair with the best-placed player sits at table 1, the next at table 2 and so on; random: pairs spread randomly, the list stays in table order.

hint.ELIMINATION: Pairs follow the bracket; the plan sets the round's scenario.

sections.title: 1. Ownership and acceptance
paragraphs: The service owner is identified only through the domain warbracket.pl. No personal details of the owner are published on this page.
By creating an account or using the application, you accept these terms. If you do not agree, you must not register or use the service.

sections.title: 2. Account and access
paragraphs: Browsing public tournaments, standings, the ranking and player profiles does not require an account. To register for tournaments, organise events, enter results or create lists, you need an account with a valid e-mail address. Keep your credentials secure and provide truthful information. You are responsible for activity performed with your account and must report unauthorised use.
We may request e-mail verification and temporarily limit access when necessary to protect the service or its users (e.g. after many failed sign-in attempts).

sections.title: Cookies and data on your device
paragraphs: The application uses only necessary technical cookies: to keep you signed in, to protect against CSRF attacks and to remember your language. We do not use analytics or advertising cookies.

So that the application works without a connection, some data (pages, tournament data, changes waiting to be sent) is stored in your browser on your device. Your account data is removed from it when you sign out.

sections.title: 3. Tournaments, results and lists
paragraphs: Organisers are responsible for running their tournaments and leagues, including settings, pairings and final results, which they may correct. Results, standings, the ELO ranking and your nickname, club and city are public. Lists are visible to the organiser and to other participants according to the tournament settings.
You must not use the service to submit illegal, deceptive, offensive or rights-infringing content, to attempt to access other accounts or data, or to disrupt the service.

sections.title: 4. Intellectual property
paragraphs: Eldfall Chronicles, its names, images and related elements belong to their respective owners. This application is an unofficial fan-made project and does not imply affiliation, sponsorship or authorisation by the game's publisher or other owners. Scenario and rule descriptions in the application are summaries, not reproductions of the rulebook.
Content you submit must respect applicable rights. By publishing a tournament, league or list, you authorise its storage and display within the application.

sections.title: 5. Availability and changes
paragraphs: The service is provided as available, without a guarantee of uninterrupted operation. We may perform maintenance, introduce changes or remove features to keep it secure and operational. We may also update these terms; the version published on this page applies from its update date.

sections.title: 6. Contact
paragraphs: For questions about these terms or the service, use the contact form available at warbracket.pl. Messages are retained as long as necessary to handle the enquiry and maintain a support history, for no longer than 12 months.

matchups.lead: Score of the row faction against the column faction. Bold: the difference from 50% is statistically significant.

units.lead: How often a character makes it into a faction's lists and how the faction does with and without it.
units.empty: No games with lists for the selected filters.
units.howToRead: The with/without difference shows the character's impact within the faction; "above exp." also removes the skill advantage of the players who field it.

roster.title: Roster vs fielded party
roster.lead: Roster-format tournaments: how often a character on the roster actually hits the table, and against whom it stays home.
roster.howToRead: Fielded = share of games in which the rostered character made the party. Opponent comparisons appear from {min} games against a faction.

items.title: Items
items.lead: How often an item makes it into a faction's lists, what it costs and whether it shows in the results.
items.empty: No games with lists for the selected filters.
items.emptyFaction: No item of this faction has enough players for the report yet.
items.costEffectLead: Horizontal: cost in points. Vertical: result above ELO expectation. Size: pick rate. Colour and label only where the difference is significant; hollow = not enough data. Underpriced items sit top left, overpriced ones bottom right.
items.inseparable: Almost always on {unit} – its effect cannot be told apart from that character.
items.deadLead: Available to the faction but picked in fewer than {share} of {n} lists.
items.noDead: Every available item is in use.
items.howToRead: With/without compares lists of the same faction. An item favoured by strong players can score high without any surplus over ELO – read the "above exp." column.

gear.title: Equipment load
gear.lead: How many items lists carry and whether heavily equipped warbands win more often than lean ones.

missions.title: Missions
missions.lead: How games are decided in each mission.
missions.empty: No games with a recorded mission.
missions.matrixLead: Faction score in each mission (mirror games excluded).

flow.title: Game flow
flow.lead: From tournament games played in detailed mode (points in every turn).
flow.empty: No games with per-turn points for the selected filters.
flow.earlyNote: lead from turn 1–2 to the end
flow.decidedTitle: From which turn the winner stays ahead
flow.vpTitle: Average VP per player per turn

schemes.title: Schemes
schemes.lead: Which scheme cards players keep, how many points they score with them and how those games end.
schemes.howToRead: A scheme that is rarely kept is seen as weak by players; one that is often kept but scores low may be a trap. Results are compared with the ELO expectation.

activity.title: Community activity
activity.lead: Games, active and new players month by month.

method.title: Methodology
method.mirrors: Mirror games (same faction on both sides) count towards a faction's share but not its score – they always give exactly 50%.
method.interval: Every score has a 95% Wilson confidence interval. Rows with fewer than {n} games are marked "not enough data".
method.elo: The expected score uses both players' ELO before the game (K = 32, start 1500), replaying all games in order.
method.privacy: Privacy: rows backed by fewer than {n} different players are left out (hidden now: {hidden}). The report never shows individual results.
method.sources: Sources: confirmed tournament games (faction and characters from the tournament list, mission from the round) and confirmed own games (faction and lists entered with the report). Item costs from the current item list (including reduced costs).

compare.splitHint: E.g. an errata date: the report shows how faction, character and item results changed between the period before that date and from it (with the other filters).
compare.title: Before and after {date}
compare.lead: Games before: {before}, from that date: {after}. Sorted by the largest change.
compare.name: Name
compare.howToRead: Change is the score difference (after − before). “Significant” means the difference exceeds the 95% error margin of both periods (two-proportion test). The share / pick column shows how popularity changed.

seasons.title: Seasons
seasons.lead: The official season ranking from tournaments the publisher marked official.
seasons.rules: Period {from} – {to}. A tournament winner gets {local} pts (local), {master} pts (master) or {international} pts (international), lower places proportionally less. A player's best {best} results count.
seasons.noResults: No finished official tournaments in this season yet.
seasons.noTournaments: No official tournaments in this period.
seasons.organizersLead: Who runs official tournaments this season.

admin.title: Official program
admin.lead: Seasons and official tournaments – for the publisher and the portal administrator.
admin.forbidden: This page is available to the game publisher and the portal administrator.
admin.name: Name
admin.formula: Points for a place = points for a win × (players − place + 1) / players. Only finished individual tournaments marked official count.
admin.confirmDelete: Delete this season? Tournaments and results stay, only the season ranking goes.
admin.officialLead: Tick the tournaments that count towards the season ranking. Changes are saved at once and logged.
admin.team: team event – does not count for the individual ranking

calendar.subscribeLead: Your phone's calendar (Google, Apple, Outlook) picks up new tournaments by itself, with the chosen filters – country and “official only”.

lists.empty: You have no saved lists yet.

lists.formatHintRoster: Roster (Season 2): no leader – you pick a party and its leader from it for every game.

lists.saveHint: Saving changes only “My lists” – lists already submitted to tournaments stay as they are.

why.formatCLASSIC: Classic, the tournament needs a roster
why.formatROSTER: a roster, the tournament is Classic

table.title: Online play
table.intro: Play Eldfall Chronicles in the browser: pick a map and a list, send your opponent the invitation link. The server checks movement, line of sight and dice; talk on Discord or similar.
table.noLists: Save a list in <link>My lists</link> first.
table.inviteReady: The table is ready. Send this link to your opponent – it works once.
table.waitingForOpponent: Waiting for the opponent to join with the invitation link.
table.terrainOverlay: Terrain as the rules see it
table.undoHint: You can only undo your own actions in this turn, before anybody rolled dice.
table.setupHelp: Pick a model and click inside your Deployment Zone (highlighted: player 1 gold, player 2 red; corner deployment uses 9″ quarter circles in opposite corners). Agree who goes first and press “Ready”.
table.pickModel: Click a model on the board to see its card.
table.movementLeft: Movement: {left}″ of {total}″ left. Click route points on the board.

stopped.BUDGET: End of movement – no inches left.
stopped.TERRAIN: Terrain taller than the model – route cut (use free movement for Climb/Jump).
stopped.ENEMY: Base contact with an enemy – movement ends.

table.endsOnAlly: Movement cannot end on an ally.

stateHelp.BLEEDING: T roll every Strategic Phase, a failure is a Wound.
stateHelp.BLINDED: No line of sight; only Assist, Dodge or Nothing.
stateHelp.CONFUSED: Half OFF, DEF, ACC, INT, AG and M.
stateHelp.CROUCHED: Hitbox = base; half SPD and ARM, STK 1; Walk only.
stateHelp.DEAD: Out of the game; gets no AP.
stateHelp.ENGAGED: In melee – limited movement and actions.
stateHelp.FATIGUED: Regains no AP; ends in its Strategic Phase.
stateHelp.FLYING: Double SPD, above terrain, always sees and is seen.
stateHelp.INCAPACITATED: HP 0: Crouched, no AP; another Wound = Dead.
stateHelp.PANICKED: M roll at the start of each activation or reaction.
stateHelp.POISONED: T roll at –6 every Strategic Phase, a failure is a Wound.
stateHelp.SHROUDED: Hidden under a token, 360° line of sight.

table.mapsIntro: Official maps, maps shared by players and your own. Build one from a background and library terrain.
table.noBackgrounds: No map backgrounds yet – an admin has to add one first.
table.mapEditorHelp: Click a library piece and drag it on the board. Rotate with the knob above the piece, Q/E or the mouse wheel; scale with the corners, +/− or Shift + wheel (Shift while dragging: 15° / 5 % steps). Scaling changes length, width and wall thickness, never height. Delete removes it. “Terrain as the rules see it” shows what blocks movement and line of sight.
table.libraryHelp: Pick a piece or a background from the list, or add a new one.
table.uploadFirst: Upload a picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 8 MB).
table.editorBoard: Picture of the piece to trace
table.drawHelp: Click points on the picture, Enter finishes the shape, Backspace removes a point, Esc cancels.
table.name: Name

toolHelp.WALL: A line along the wall; set its thickness and height.
toolHelp.OBSTACLE: Outline of a solid (rock, house); blocks models shorter than it.
toolHelp.AREA: Outline of an Environment (forest, water…); models walk on it.

table.retireHelp: A retired piece disappears from the map editor but stays on saved maps and in games.
table.endProposedByYou: Waiting for the opponent to agree to end the game.
table.reported: Result reported – the opponent confirms it in <link>My games</link>.
table.reportResult: Report the result as an own game
table.reportHelp: The Victory Points result and both lists go to My games; once the opponent confirms, it counts for ELO, leagues and statistics.
table.sprayNeedsModel: Pick the model using the Spray template first.
table.tokenHelp: Click the board to put a token down; click a token to select it.
table.tokenMoveHelp: Click the new spot to move the selected token.
table.sprayHelp: Pick the attacking model, then click the direction – the narrow end touches its base.
table.circleHelp: Click the centre of the template. The selected model (the user) does not suffer its own Attack.

measureHelp.ASSISTED: Any distance may be pre-measured (ruler, ranges, route length).
measureHelp.STANDARD: Pre-measuring only within the Awareness of your models and the activated model's Movement; while moving only the Movement. Templates are not pre-measured before placing.
measureHelp.REALISM: No pre-measuring: distances are checked only after a Movement or Action is declared. A move that is too long ends at the model's limit.

table.realismMove: Realism mode: mark the route – the model only goes as far as its Movement allows.
table.sharingHelp: A link is shown only once. A new link cancels the previous one.
table.observersHelp: With the link they watch the game live, without any influence on it. Switching off removes their access at once.
table.judgeHelp: The judge may move, turn and mark all models, enter points, end the game and undo any number of steps – also after dice rolls.
table.linksOnce: Copy the links now – new ones can be generated later in the table panel.

joinAsHelp.JUDGE: You become the judge of this game: you can correct models and undo the players' steps.
joinAsHelp.WATCH: You will watch the game live, without being able to interfere.

placingHelp.MODEL: Click on the board to place: {name}. Esc to stop.
